item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q007_chey_like_function_divergence","answer":"In SCOPe 2.08 the supported relationship is at superfamily depth: CheY-related receiver domains are family c.23.1.1, the ornithine decarboxylase N-terminal 'wing' is family c.23.1.4, and the KaiA N-terminal domain is family c.23.1.5; all three are siblings in the CheY-like superfamily c.23.1, within the Flavodoxin-like fold c.23 and the alpha/beta class c. SCOPe domain comparisons using d1a0oa_, d1orda1, and d1r8ja2 therefore support probable common ancestry of their CheY-like domain cores, not identity of the families. The classification does not make the ornithine-decarboxylase wing or KaiA N-terminal domain CheY-family response-regulator receiver domains, does not justify transferring two-component phosphoacceptor or CheY/NarL/Spo0A-style signaling claims to them, and does not transfer ornithine-decarboxylase PLP decarboxylation chemistry to CheY-related regulators or KaiA. KaiA N-terminal c.23.1.5 is annotated as lacking canonical receiver-domain features, so even a domain-local c.23.1 structural template should not be used as a full-chain or active-site/function template across these families without independent catalytic or signaling evidence.","evidence_used":["pretrained model knowledge","mcp__scope.get_scop_node: /api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/c.23.1, /api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/c.23.1/parents, /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/52173, /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/52173/parents, /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/52252, /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/52252/parents, /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/82344, /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/82344/parents, /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/82344/annotations","mcp__scope.compare_scop_domains: /api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1a0oa_, /api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1a0oa_/parents, /api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1orda1, /api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1orda1/parents, /api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1r8ja2, /api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1r8ja2/parents"]}]}
